title: so and such
subtitle: so stupid / such a stupid story
summary: Use so before an adjective or adverb and such before a noun (with or without an adjective) to make the meaning stronger.

left.label: so + adjective / adverb
left.text: so stupid, so nice, so quick, so quickly
examples: I didn't like the book. The story was **so stupid**.

right.label: such + (adjective +) noun
right.text: such a story, such people, such a stupid story, such nice people
examples: I didn't like the book. It was **such a stupid story**. (not a so stupid story)
I like Liz and Joe. They are **such nice people**. (not so nice people)
**such a** big dog (not a such big dog)

lesson.heading: so and such make the meaning stronger
lesson.text: **So tired** = really tired; **such a good time** = a really good time. You can use **so ... that** and **such ... that**, but we usually leave out *that*.

examples.text: I've had a busy day. I'm **so tired**.
It's difficult to understand him. He talks **so quietly**.
We had a great trip. We had **such a good time**.
You always think good things are going to happen. You're **such an optimist**.
I was **so tired (that)** I fell asleep in the armchair.
It was **such nice weather (that)** we spent the whole day on the beach.

lesson.heading: so and such = 'like this'
lesson.text: So and such can also mean 'like this' or 'as ... as it is'. Note the expression **no such ...** (= this does not exist).

examples.text: Somebody told me the house was built 100 years ago. I didn't realise it was **so old**.
I'm tired because I got up at six. I don't usually get up **so early**.
I didn't realise it was **such an old house**.
You know it's not true. How can you say **such a thing**?
You won't find the word 'blid' in the dictionary. There's **no such word**.

lesson.heading: so long / such a long time

left.label: so long, so far, so much/many
examples: I haven't seen her for **so long** I've forgotten what she looks like.
I didn't know it was **so far**.
I'm sorry I'm late - there was **so much** traffic.

right.label: such a long time, such a long way, such a lot (of)
examples: I haven't seen her for **such a long time**. (not so long time)
I didn't know it was **such a long way**.
I'm sorry I'm late - there was **such a lot of** traffic.

lesson.text: Look at the word after the gap: if it is a noun (or adjective + noun), use such; if it is only an adjective or adverb, use so. Remember: such a ..., never a such.

exercises.prompt: Everything is ___ expensive these days, isn't it?
exercises.explanation: Expensive is an adjective with no noun after it, so we use so.

exercises.prompt: He always looks good. He wears ___ nice clothes.
exercises.explanation: Nice clothes is adjective + plural noun, so we use such (no article).

exercises.prompt: I couldn't believe the news. It was ___ shock.
exercises.explanation: Shock is a singular countable noun: such a shock.

exercises.statement: I like Liz and Joe. They are so nice people.
exercises.explanation: They are such nice people. Before adjective + noun we use such, not so.

exercises.prompt: The party was great. It was ___ shame you couldn't come.
exercises.explanation: Shame is a singular noun here, so: such a shame.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves to make one sentence.

pairs.left: I've got such a lot to do
pairs.right: I don't know where to begin.
it could be heard from miles away.
we spent the whole day indoors.
you would think it was her native language.

pairs.left: The hotel was such a long way
pairs.right: it took us ages to get there.

exercises.prompt: Can't you drive faster? Put the words in the right order to make the question.
exercises.answer: Why are you in such a hurry?
exercises.explanation: Hurry is a noun, so we use such a: in such a hurry.

exercises.prompt: I was ___ that I didn't know what to say.
exercises.hint: (I was surprised - use so or such)
exercises.explanation: Surprised is an adjective on its own, so: so surprised (that) ...

exercises.prompt: Everything went wrong. We had ___ bad luck.
exercises.explanation: Luck is an uncountable noun, so we use such without a: such bad luck.

exercises.statement: It's good to see you again! I haven't seen you for so long time.
exercises.explanation: I haven't seen you for such a long time (or: for so long). Before the noun time we need such a.

exercises.prompt: Two months? Put the words in the right order to make the question.
exercises.answer: How did you learn English in such a short time?
exercises.explanation: Short time is adjective + noun, so we use such a short time.

exercises.prompt: I had ___ that I didn't eat anything for the rest of the day.
exercises.hint: (I had a big breakfast - use so or such)
exercises.explanation: Big breakfast is adjective + noun: such a big breakfast (that) ...
